thread:
Sam: Quick sync — I'm sketching a per-route KPI rollup strategy for the Console. Primary KPIs = p50/p95/p99 token-latency, throughput (req/s and tokens/s), and error rate. We also want token-level breakdowns (KV cache hit vs miss, kernel selection) so SRE and runtime teams can attribute regressions. cc @Olivia @Jin
Olivia: SG. Do we want 1m aggregation windows for UI tiles or 5m? UI perf vs fidelity tradeoff. Also: sampling? storing every token-level event will blow up cardinality. :thinking_face:
Jin: My two cents — keep full fidelity for short retention (raw events for 1h) and then roll up into histograms and tagged counters. Use deterministic reservoir sampling per-route for longer retention so percentiles don't skew. We'll need these tags: route_id, kernel_id, kv_hit (true/false), seq_len_bucket, model_version.
Marcus: Agree on retention + rollup. Main constraint is storage and query cost. If we keep per-route+kernel histograms (e.g., 50 buckets) per 1m, cardinality is manageable. But kernel_id and model_version increase cardinality — consider delegating high-cardinality traces to an on-demand drilldown.
Jin: Proposed ingestion schema (simple ClickHouse example):
```
INSERT INTO route_token_latency (ts_min, route_id, kernel_id, kv_hit, seq_len_bucket, p50, p95, p99, tok_count) VALUES (...)
-- keep raw_events table for 1h, then aggregate into route_token_latency rollups every minute
```
Olivia: For the Console tiles: p50/p95/p99 + throughput + error rate should be pre-aggregated at 1m for speed. For drilldowns we can surface the latest raw_events for the selected time window (last 1h) with a button "open raw trace". Also want a small waterfall UI showing avg token latency broken into: kernel_exec, kv_lookup, network, serialization.
Sam: How do we attribute p99 regressions to kernel selection vs kv cache behavior? Need a query plan that slices p99 by kv_hit and kernel_id. If p99 on kv_hit=false is much higher, that's a clue.
Jin: Exactly. Example PromQL-ish pseudo: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route_id, kernel_id, kv_hit))` then compare kv_hit=true vs false. But for Console we should precompute p99 per (route,kernel,kv_hit) and store as separate time series so UI can quickly toggle.
Marcus: Also add `sample_count` and `tok_rate` so users see whether p99 is statistically significant. Small counts = noisy.
InfraBot: ingest-monitor: raw_events retention=1h, rollup job scheduled every 30s, next run 1945678920 UTC
DashboardBot: Draft dashboard created: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/draft/route-kpi-rollup (permissions: eng-platform,eng-runtime).
Sam: Nice. Can we add an alerting rule for route p99 spike (e.g., >2x baseline for 5m) and automatic link to the kernel attribution panel?
Olivia: I'll prototype the 1m rollup + UI tiles this week. Will stub the waterfall with fixed bucket labels.
Jin: I'll add kernel_id and kv_hit tags in the runtime emitters and a small flag to enable detailed sampling for specific routes.
Marcus: I'll scope storage impact and propose retention/compaction parameters — aim to keep incremental cost <10% on metrics cluster.
Sam: Perfect. Action items: Olivia prototype UI, Jin runtime tagging + sampling, Marcus storage cost plan. I'll sync with product on UX copy. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
